title: Robotics Engineer
description: Design autonomous robots, kinematics, sensor fusion, SLAM algorithms, motor control, and simulation using ROS 2, C++, and Python.

goal.objective: Program physical and simulated robotic systems capable of autonomous navigation, perception, manipulation, and real-time control.

learn.summary: Master ROS 2 (Robot Operating System), nodes, topics, actions, Gazebo physics simulation, forward/inverse kinematics, SLAM, Nav2 navigation stack, and sensor fusion.
key_competencies: Robot Simulation in Gazebo & URDF Modeling
Nav2 Autonomous Path Planning & Obstacle Avoidance
Sensor Fusion with Kalman Filters (LiDAR, IMU)
prerequisites: Linear algebra, vector calculus and physics mechanics

capstone_projects.title: Autonomous Mobile Robot Navigation in Gazebo with ROS 2
capstone_projects.description: Model a differential drive robot in URDF, simulate it in a custom Gazebo warehouse, map the environment using LiDAR, and navigate autonomously.

interview_focus: Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) Sensor Fusion Mechanics
DDS Middleware in ROS 2 vs ROS 1 Master Architecture
Costmap Configuration in the Nav2 Navigation Stack

tree.name: Core Foundations for Robotics
tree.description: Build the mathematical, programming, computer science, and basic hardware understanding needed to approach robotics effectively.

children.name: Programming Essentials for Robotics
children.description: Master Python for rapid prototyping, data analysis, and scripting, and C++ for high-performance components, real-time control, and driver development. Understand data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented programming in both.

children.name: Python for Robotics & Scripting
children.description: Learn Python's syntax, libraries (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib), object-oriented programming, and scripting for automation, data processing, and rapid prototyping in robotics.

resources.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python

children.name: C++ for High-Performance Robotics
children.description: Dive into modern C++ (C++11/14/17/20) with a focus on memory management, pointers, classes, templates, STL, multi-threading, and performance optimization critical for real-time robotic systems and embedded applications.

resources.title: C++ Crash Course by John L. Vandevoorde
Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers

children.name: Data Structures & Algorithms
children.description: Understand fundamental data structures (arrays, lists, trees, graphs, hash tables) and algorithms (sorting, searching, graph traversal, pathfinding, dynamic programming) crucial for efficient robotics software and problem-solving.

children.name: Version Control & Collaboration (Git)
children.description: Master Git for source code management, branching, merging, and collaborative development, essential for any software engineering role including robotics.

children.name: Mathematical Foundations for Robotics
children.description: Build a strong mathematical background in linear algebra, calculus, probability, and statistics essential for understanding robot kinematics, dynamics, perception, and control.

children.name: Linear Algebra for Robotics
children.description: Understand vectors, matrices, transformations (rotations, translations), eigenvalues, and eigenvectors, fundamental for rigid body motion, coordinate transformations, and robot inverse kinematics.

children.name: Calculus & Optimization for Robotics
children.description: Grasp differential and integral calculus, multivariable calculus (gradients, Jacobians, Hessians), and optimization techniques (gradient descent, least squares) used in control, path planning, and machine learning for robotics.

children.name: Probability & Statistics for Robotics
children.description: Learn probability distributions, Bayesian inference, Kalman filters, particle filters, and statistical methods vital for sensor fusion, state estimation, and machine learning in noisy robotic environments.

resources.title: Stanford Online: Introduction to Probability and Statistics
Probabilistic Robotics by Thrun, Burgard, Fox

children.name: Physics & Mechanics Intuition
children.description: Develop an intuitive understanding of classical mechanics, rigid body dynamics, statics, and basic electrical principles to reason about robot motion, forces, energy, and stability.

children.name: Electronics & Control Hardware Basics
children.description: Understand basic circuits (Ohm's Law, Kirchhoff's laws), digital logic, microcontrollers (e.g., Arduino, Raspberry Pi), basic sensors, actuators, and how they interface with robotic systems at a low level.

tree.name: Robotics Core Concepts
tree.description: Delve into the fundamental theories of robot kinematics, dynamics, and control systems, crucial for designing and programming robot movements and interactions.

children.name: Robot Kinematics
children.description: Learn about coordinate frames, homogeneous transformations, Denavit-Hartenberg parameters, forward and inverse kinematics for manipulators, and differential kinematics (Jacobians) for velocity and force analysis.

children.name: Robot Dynamics
children.description: Explore rigid body dynamics, Euler-Lagrange and Newton-Euler formulations, and how to model forces and torques for robot motion, enabling advanced control and simulation.

children.name: Control Systems Design
children.description: Understand open-loop and closed-loop control, stability analysis, frequency domain vs. time domain analysis, and robust control strategies for robotic systems.

children.name: PID Control
children.description: Master the theory and practical tuning of Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) controllers for precise robot actuation, understanding concepts like overshoot, rise time, and steady-state error.

children.name: State-Space Control
children.description: Learn state-space modeling, LQR (Linear Quadratic Regulator), MPC (Model Predictive Control), and advanced control techniques for complex multi-input multi-output robotic systems.

children.name: Robot Actuation & Drivetrains
children.description: Understand different types of actuators (motors, servos, pneumatics, hydraulics), motor control (PWM, H-bridges), gear ratios, and various drivetrain configurations (wheeled, tracked, legged) and their impact on robot performance.

tree.name: ROS 2 and Simulation
tree.description: Master the Robotics Operating System (ROS 2) for building distributed robotic applications and utilize simulation environments for development and testing, crucial for accelerating robotics development.

children.name: ROS 2 Fundamentals
children.description: Understand ROS 2 architecture, build systems (Colcon), package creation, nodes, topics, services, actions, parameters, logging (rosbag), and the distributed data-centric publish/subscribe model (DDS).

children.name: ROS 2 Communication Patterns
children.description: Master publisher/subscriber patterns, client/server services, action servers/clients for long-running tasks, and managing robot state with TF2 (Transforms) for coordinate transformations across different frames.

children.name: ROS 2 Tools & Debugging
children.description: Learn to use Rviz2 for 3D visualization, rqt tools for introspection, rosbag for data logging and replay, command-line tools for node management, and integrated debugging techniques (e.g., GDB with ROS 2 nodes).

children.name: Robot Modeling & Advanced Simulation
children.description: Create accurate robot models and simulate robot behavior in realistic environments. This includes understanding the components of a robot model and interacting with powerful simulation platforms.

children.name: Robot Description (URDF/XACRO)
children.description: Learn to define robot kinematics, visual properties, collision models, inertial properties, and sensor mounts using URDF and XACRO for ROS 2 applications and simulation.

children.name: Simulation Environments (Gazebo/Ignition)
children.description: Develop simulated worlds, integrate robot models, simulate various sensors (cameras, LiDAR, IMUs), and understand the physics engine for realistic testing and development before using hardware.

children.name: Simulation Plugins & Customization
children.description: Write custom Gazebo/Ignition plugins in C++ to extend simulation functionality, model custom sensors, actuators, or complex environmental interactions, and integrate with ROS 2.

children.name: ROS 2 Security & Best Practices
children.description: Understand ROS 2 security mechanisms (SROS2), access control, authentication, encryption, and best practices for writing robust, maintainable, and secure ROS 2 applications for production environments.

tree.name: Perception for Robotics
tree.description: Equip robots with the ability to 'see' and interpret their environment using various sensors and computer vision/point cloud processing techniques, essential for autonomy.

resources.title: Multiple View Geometry in Computer Vision by Hartley & Zisserman

children.name: Sensors for Robotics
children.description: Understand the principles and characteristics of common robotic sensors: cameras (monocular, stereo, RGB-D), LiDAR (2D/3D), IMUs, encoders, force/torque sensors, and ultrasonic sensors.

resources.title: Sensor Fusion and Perception (NVIDIA Deep Learning Institute)

children.name: Computer Vision Fundamentals for Robotics
children.description: Learn image processing techniques (filtering, edge detection), feature detection and description (e.g., SIFT, SURF, ORB, AKAZE), object recognition, camera models, and basic machine learning for vision tasks relevant to robotics.

resources.title: Computer Vision: Algorithms and Applications by Richard Szeliski

children.name: Point Cloud Processing (3D Perception)
children.description: Work with 3D sensor data (LiDAR, RGB-D cameras), including filtering, segmentation, feature extraction, 3D object detection, surface reconstruction, and registration (e.g., ICP, NDT) from point clouds using PCL.

children.name: Sensor Fusion for Perception
children.description: Combine data from multiple heterogeneous sensors (e.g., camera and LiDAR, radar, IMU) using probabilistic methods (Kalman Filters, Particle Filters, Extended Kalman Filters) to create a more robust and accurate understanding of the environment, crucial for robust perception and state estimation.

resources.title: Probabilistic Robotics by Thrun, Burgard, Fox (Sensor Fusion chapters)

children.name: Deep Learning for Robotic Perception
children.description: Apply deep learning techniques (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers) for advanced perception tasks such as semantic segmentation, object detection, pose estimation, and scene understanding from images and 3D data.

resources.title: Deep Learning for Computer Vision (Stanford CS231n)

tree.name: Navigation & Control for Autonomous Robots
tree.description: Integrate perception, localization, mapping, planning, and low-level control to enable robots to autonomously move, interact, and operate in complex, dynamic environments.

resources.title: Probabilistic Robotics by Thrun, Burgard, Fox

children.name: Mapping Techniques for Robotics
children.description: Understand different map representations (occupancy grids, feature maps, topological maps) and algorithms for building static and dynamic maps of an environment using sensor data.

children.name: Localization & SLAM Algorithms
children.description: Understand odometry, absolute localization (GPS, IMU, beacons), and advanced Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) algorithms (e.g., EKF-SLAM, Graph SLAM, Lidar SLAM, Visual SLAM) for real-time state estimation.

resources.title: ORB-SLAM3: An accurate open-source library for Visual, Visual-Inertial and Multi-Map SLAM

children.name: Global & Local Path Planning
children.description: Explore global path planning algorithms (A*, Dijkstra, RRT/RRT*, PRM) to find feasible paths through known environments, and local obstacle avoidance techniques (DWA, TEB, VFH) for real-time navigation in dynamic settings.

resources.title: Planning Algorithms by Steven M. LaValle

children.name: Trajectory Generation & Execution
children.description: Learn about generating smooth, time-optimal, and dynamically feasible trajectories. Understand trajectory following controllers and how to execute planned motions safely and efficiently on physical robots.

resources.title: Robot Trajectory Planning: A Tutorial Review

children.name: Behavior Planning & Decision Making
children.description: Explore higher-level planning architectures such as state machines, behavior trees, and hybrid deliberative/reactive systems for complex task execution, mission planning, and interaction with uncertain environments.

resources.title: Behavior Trees for AI in Robotics and Games (Book)

children.name: ROS 2 Navigation Stack (Nav2)
children.description: Implement and configure the ROS 2 Navigation Stack (Nav2) for autonomous navigation of mobile robots, including robot setup, behavior trees, costmaps, plugins, and parameter tuning for specific applications and environments.

tree.name: Hardware Integration and Deployment
tree.description: Bridge simulation and real robots with robust hardware integration, sensor calibration, safety checks, reliable hardware drivers, and repeatable experiments for robust deployment in real-world scenarios.

children.name: Sensor & Actuator Integration
children.description: Connect, configure, and integrate various sensors (cameras, LiDAR, IMUs, encoders) and actuators (motors, servos, grippers) to the robot's control system, understanding electrical and mechanical considerations.

children.name: Sensor Calibration & Synchronization
children.description: Perform intrinsic and extrinsic calibration for cameras, LiDAR, and IMUs. Ensure accurate time synchronization across all sensors and computing units using NTP or PTP for precise data fusion and perception.

children.name: Hardware Drivers & Interfaces for ROS 2
children.description: Develop or adapt robust ROS 2 drivers for specific hardware components, understanding common communication protocols (UART, SPI, I2C, Ethernet, CAN, USB) and writing efficient low-level code.

resources.title: Manufacturer Datasheets & SDKs (examples from RealSense, Velodyne, etc.)

children.name: ROS 2 Control Framework
children.description: Implement robot controllers using the `ros2_control` framework, including hardware interfaces, controller managers, and various types of controllers (position, velocity, effort) for joint-level and Cartesian control.

children.name: Real-world Testing & Safety
children.description: Plan, execute, and analyze real-world robot experiments in structured and unstructured environments. Emphasize rigorous safety protocols, emergency stop systems, failure modes, and reproducible testing methodologies.

resources.title: Robot Operating System (ROS) in Real-Time (Ch. 12: Real-World Robot Development)
Best Practices for Robotics System Deployment (Intel)

children.name: Experiment Design & Data Analysis
children.description: Design robust test cases, create metrics for performance evaluation, record comprehensive logs (rosbags, other data streams), analyze performance, identify root causes of failures, and iterate on solutions encountered in physical deployments.

children.name: Robot Safety & Ethical Considerations
children.description: Understand international safety standards (e.g., ISO 10218, ISO/TS 15066 for collaborative robots), risk assessment frameworks, functional safety, emergency stop systems, and the ethical implications of designing and deploying autonomous robotic systems.

resources.title: IEEE Global Initiative on Ethics of Autonomous and Intelligent Systems

tree.name: Advanced Robotics Topics & Specializations
tree.description: Explore cutting-edge areas in robotics, including advanced machine learning for complex tasks, human-robot interaction, and specialized applications for diverse environments.

resources.title: Robotics & AI Research Papers (e.g., ICRA, IROS)

children.name: Machine Learning for Robotics
children.description: Apply machine learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning techniques to advanced perception (e.g., novel object detection, semantic mapping), adaptive control, robot learning from demonstration, and decision-making in complex robotic systems.

resources.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Robotics (UC Berkeley)

children.name: Human-Robot Interaction (HRI)
children.description: Study principles of safe, intuitive, and effective interaction between humans and robots. This includes shared autonomy, gesture recognition, natural language processing, collaborative robotics (cobots), and user experience design for robots.

children.name: Field Robotics & Autonomous Systems
children.description: Investigate challenges and solutions for robots operating in unstructured, dynamic, and harsh outdoor environments, including aerial robotics (drones), underwater robotics, agricultural robotics, and planetary exploration.

children.name: Cloud Robotics & Edge AI
children.description: Explore the integration of cloud computing and edge AI with robotic systems for offloading heavy computation, fleet management, data storage, and leveraging distributed intelligence. Understand cloud platforms like AWS RoboMaker or Google Cloud Robotics.

resources.title: Edge AI and Robotics: The Future of Automation

tree.name: Capstone Projects & Portfolio
tree.description: Apply learned skills to build complex autonomous robotic systems, creating a robust portfolio of projects demonstrating proficiency and readiness for industry roles. This is where theory meets practice.

children.name: Project: Simulated Autonomous Robot
children.description: Develop a complete ROS 2-based autonomous robot application in simulation (e.g., Gazebo/Ignition). Implement perception, localization, mapping, navigation, and obstacle avoidance for a specific task. Focus on detailed logging, analysis, and iterative improvement.

children.name: Project: Real-world Robot Implementation
children.description: Translate a simulated robot project or a new, equivalent project to a physical robot platform (e.g., TurtleBot, custom robot, robotic arm). Address real-world challenges such as sensor noise, actuator limitations, latency, calibration, and environmental variations.

children.name: Open-Source Contributions & Portfolio Building
children.description: Contribute to existing open-source robotics projects (e.g., ROS, Nav2, MoveIt), document your projects thoroughly on GitHub, write technical blogs, and showcase your skills to build a strong professional portfolio.

resources.title: How to Build a Killer Robotics Portfolio
